_description: Example: D-grade listing. Everything needs work. Shows how BCS prioritizes when gaps are everywhere.
_dog: Shadow — 7yr black lab mix, 6 months in rescue, black dog syndrome risk

dimensions.gap: No personality. 'Sweet and gentle' — every dog in every rescue in the country.
Single kennel photo. Black dog on gray floor under fluorescent light. Invisible.
Good with dogs mentioned. Nothing else.
Age (7) not reframed. Black dog not acknowledged. 6 months in rescue not addressed — adopter will wonder why.
No coached story. No strong asset identified.
Faint picture — not enough to close.

bcs_score.coaching_summary: Shadow is invisible right now. Black dog, kennel photo, fluorescent light — this listing is working against her. The photo is the emergency. Get her outside, get her eye contact, and find the one thing only her foster knows. Everything else follows.

coaching_actions_triggered: Go outside or near a window. Fluorescent light kills personality.
Wait for eye contact. Don't take the shot until the dog is looking at the camera.
Ask the foster: 'Tell me about the last time Shadow made you laugh.'
Reframe the age: 'Shadow is seven — which means she's done with the chaos and ready to just be your dog.'
Address the 6 months: 'She's been patient. She deserves a sentence that says so.'
